A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LazyDrag with the same authors, method, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original DragBench evaluations, a 20-participant user study, component ablations, and qualitative experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results, reports a revised 32-participant user study, and adds runtime and memory measurements in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: The explicit correspondence map, winner-takes-all displacement fusion, Gaussian latent initialization, background token replacement, identity preservation, and gated attention refinement remain unchanged. The added optimized configuration changes evaluation settings rather than introducing an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same DragBench coverage: 205 images and 349 handle-target pairs, alongside retained drag, move/scale, text-guided, and multi-round examples. Runtime profiling uses the existing benchmark; the larger expert sample does not introduce a different population.

E2.justification: The eight named editing baselines in Tables 1 and 2 are retained. New runtime Table 6 compares against DragText and FastDrag and adds an evaluated Normal Generation control. Newly cited LightningDrag and ConsistEdit are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The reported user-study sample increases from 20 to 32 experts, retaining 32 cases; Figure 13 changes from eight displayed alternatives to nine, although both versions' Table 2 already lists nine methods. Appendix B.4 adds runtime/memory evaluation and a 20-step, 0.7-inversion configuration alongside the retained 50-step, full-inversion setting.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 adds analysis of computational overhead through inversion, correspondence-map generation, synthesis timing, and memory measurements under default and optimized settings. Existing component ablations, activation-timestep sensitivity, U-Net adaptation, text-guidance examples, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three evaluations per benchmark metric and report means and standard deviations. The new timing results continue mean-plus/minus reporting without specifying a new repetition or uncertainty-estimation procedure. Changed preference values and participant counts do not establish a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3–5 retain their numerical results. Table 2 revises preferences under the changed user-study setting, including LazyDrag from 61.88±19 to 63.67±16. New Table 6 reports, among other measurements, LazyDrag at 14.10 seconds and 62 GB by default versus 4.31 seconds and 49 GB under the optimized configuration.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the same correspondence definitions, displacement calculations, latent construction, attention updates, and move/scale formulation. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of MM-DiT drag editing with explicit correspondence, stable full-strength inversion without test-time optimization, text-guided control, and superior benchmark performance. The extra introduction bullet repeats existing text-guidance and preservation claims rather than adding a distinct contribution.

C2.justification: New runtime discussion attributes computational cost primarily to the MM-DiT backbone, explains amortizing inversion across subsequent edits, and discusses acceleration opportunities and low-latency use. Existing limitations concerning overlapping targets, small drags, and dependence on the base model are unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds bfloat16 precision disclosure, detailed computational-resource measurements, and configuration information for runtime profiling. It also promises public code release upon acceptance; the PDFs do not establish that release occurred. The project link, H800 hardware disclosure, and principal implementation instructions were already present.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to ConsistEdit, LightningDrag, and xDiT. Section 3.1.3 more explicitly distinguishes LazyDrag from naively combining FastDrag and CharaConsist, and Appendix A.1 adds a rationale for excluding DragGAN. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, with localized abstract and Section 3.1.3 revisions. v3 adds ethics, reproducibility, runtime-analysis, and LLM-usage sections. It also introduces a duplicated contribution bullet while retaining the description of the contributions as threefold.

P2.justification: The document switches from a two-column ACM-style layout to a single-column ICLR layout, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. Figure 1's incorrect pipeline caption is replaced with an appropriate description, Figure 13's study interface is revised, and Table 6 is added. Former Figures 8 and 12 are exchanged in numbering and placement, with their examples retained.

improvement.justification: The runtime and memory analysis makes practical costs assessable, including substantial memory requirements previously unquantified, and the corrected Figure 1 caption fixes a clear presentation error. These provide a limited net improvement. Benefits are tempered by the stale 61.88% preference statement beside Table 2's 63.67%, and by claiming superior optimized-setting quality without corresponding quality measurements.
